summary: Some very deep and holy parts of the Torah may be taught only to a few students at a time, and only to a wise student. A person must not try to dig into things Hashem did not let us know.

chunks.en: We do not teach the hidden halachos of forbidden relationships to three students together,
chunks.st: One may not expound the topic of forbidden sexual relations before three or more individuals;

words.note: Relatives a person may not marry.

chunks.en: nor the secrets of how Hashem created the world to two,
chunks.st: nor may one expound the act of Creation and the secrets of the beginning of the world before two or more individuals;

chunks.en: nor the Merkavah even to one student,
chunks.explain: The Merkavah is a very holy, secret vision of Hashem's "chariot."
chunks.st: nor may one expound by oneself the Design of the Divine Chariot, a mystical teaching with regard to the ways God conducts the world,

words.note: The vision of Hashem's chariot that the navi Yechezkel saw.

chunks.en: unless he is
chunks.st: unless he is

chunks.en: wise and understands things on his own.
chunks.st: wise and understands most matters on his own.

chunks.en: Anyone who looks into four things,
chunks.st: The mishna continues in the same vein: Whoever looks at four matters,

chunks.he: רָאוּי לוֹ כְּאִלּוּ לֹא בָּא לָעוֹלָם,
chunks.en: it would be better for him if he had not come into the world:
chunks.st: it would have been better for him had he never entered the world:

chunks.en: what is above the sky,
chunks.st: Anyone who reflects upon what is above the firmament

chunks.en: what is below the earth,
chunks.st: and what is below the earth,

chunks.en: what was before the world was made,
chunks.st: what was before Creation,

chunks.en: and what will be after the world ends.
chunks.st: and what will be after the end of the world.

chunks.he: וְכָל שֶׁלֹּא חָס עַל כְּבוֹד קוֹנוֹ,
chunks.en: And anyone who does not care about the honor of his Creator,
chunks.st: And anyone who has no concern for the honor of his Maker,
chunks.stMore: who inquires into and deals with matters not permitted to him,

chunks.en: it would be better for him if he had not come into the world.
chunks.st: deserves to have never come to the world.

summary: This mishnah lists the pairs of great Rabbis who led the Jewish people, and how each one ruled about doing semichah, leaning one's hands on a korban, on Yom Tov.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
chunks.en: Yosei ben Yoezer says not to do semichah on Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: Semichah is leaning your hands on a korban before it is shechted.
chunks.st: Yosei ben Yo’ezer says not to place one’s hands on offerings before slaughtering them on a Festival
chunks.stMore: because this is considered performing labor with an animal on a Festival.

words.note: To lean hands on a korban (semichah).

chunks.en: Yosei ben Yochanan says to do semichah.
chunks.st: His colleague, Yosef ben Yoḥanan, says to place them;

chunks.he: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן פְּרַחְיָה אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
chunks.en: Yehoshua ben Perachyah says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Yehoshua ben Peraḥya says not to place them;

chunks.en: Nitai HaArbeli says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Nitai HaArbeli says to place them;

chunks.he: יְהוּדָה בֶּן טַבַּאי אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא לִסְמוֹךְ,
chunks.en: Yehudah ben Tabai says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Yehuda ben Tabbai says not to place them;

chunks.en: Shimon ben Shatach says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Shimon ben Shataḥ says to place them;

chunks.en: Shemayah says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Shemaya says to place them;

chunks.en: Avtalyon says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Avtalyon says not to place them.

chunks.en: Hillel and Menachem did not argue.
chunks.st: Hillel and Menaḥem did not disagree with regard to this issue.

chunks.en: Menachem left his job,
chunks.st: Menaḥem departed from his post,

chunks.en: and Shammai came in his place.
chunks.st: and Shammai entered in his stead.

chunks.en: Shammai says not to do semichah.
chunks.st: Shammai says not to place them;

chunks.en: Hillel says to do semichah.
chunks.st: Hillel says to place them.

chunks.en: The first one of each pair was the Nasi,
chunks.st: The first members of each pair served as Nasi,

words.note: The Nasi was the head of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: and the second one was the Av Beis Din, the next in charge.
chunks.st: and their counterparts served as deputy Nasi.

words.note: Av Beis Din: the second leader of the Sanhedrin.

summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about which korbanos may be brought on Yom Tov, and whether we may lean our hands on them.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: We may bring shelamim on Yom Tov, but we do not do semichah on them,
chunks.st: One may bring peace-offerings on a Festival because both the owners and the priests partake of them, but one may not place his hands on them,
chunks.stMore: on the peace-offerings before sacrificing them.

chunks.en: but we may not bring olos.
chunks.explain: Olos are not eaten, and on Yom Tov we work only to make food.
chunks.st: However, one may not bring burnt-offerings
chunks.stMore: at all because they are not eaten, and labor is permitted on Festivals only for the sake of preparing food for humans.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: We may bring shelamim and olos, and we do semichah on them.
chunks.st: One may bring peace-offerings and also burnt-offerings, and one places his hands on both of them.

summary: When Shavuos comes on Erev Shabbos or on Shabbos, the Yom Tov korbanos may be brought on Sunday. On that Sunday the Kohen Gadol did not wear his special clothes, to show that Shavuos is not always on Sunday.

chunks.en: When Shavuos falls on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the festival of Shavuot occurs on the eve of Shabbat,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: the day for shechting the korbanos is after Shabbos.
chunks.explain: They hold the Yom Tov olah is not brought on Yom Tov itself.
chunks.st: The day of slaughter is after Shabbat, on Sunday.
chunks.stMore: This is the day on which the animals brought in honor of the pilgrim Festival are slaughtered, since they maintain that the Festival burnt-offering is not sacrificed on the Festival day itself but on the following day, and all burnt-offerings vowed by individuals are postponed to the following day.

words.note: The day the Yom Tov korbanos are brought.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: There is no shechting day after Shabbos.
chunks.explain: The korbanos may be brought on Yom Tov itself.
chunks.st: The day of slaughter is not after Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: Since the slaughter may be performed on the Festival day itself, it is unnecessary to postpone it.

chunks.en: But they agree that if Shavuos falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: But they concede that if Shavuot occurs on Shabbat,

chunks.en: the shechting day is after Shabbos.
chunks.st: the day of slaughter is after Shabbat.

chunks.en: On that day the Kohen Gadol does not put on his special clothes,
chunks.st: The mishna relates that when the day of slaughter was on a Sunday, the High Priest would not dress in his festive garments
chunks.stMore: but would wear his regular clothing.

words.note: The Kohen Gadol is the head Kohen.

chunks.en: and people may give hespedim and fast on it,
chunks.st: And all were permitted to eulogize and fast on this day.

words.note: A speech of sadness for someone who died.

chunks.en: so as not to support the words of those who say
chunks.explain: These were people who did not believe in the Torah she'baal peh.
chunks.st: This was done in order not to uphold and reinforce the opinion of the Sadducees, who would say:

chunks.en: Shavuos is always after Shabbos.
chunks.st: Shavuot must always occur after Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: As the day of slaughter was on Sunday, it was necessary to demonstrate that we do not accept the view of the Sadducees, and that the day is not a Festival.

summary: There are different levels of tahara for different kinds of holy food. For regular food we wash our hands, but for korbanos we dip our hands in a mikveh.

chunks.en: We wash hands for regular food, for maaser, and for terumah.
chunks.st: One must wash his hands by pouring a quarter-log of water over them before eating non-sacred food, and for tithes and for teruma;

chunks.en: But for korbanos, we dip the hands in a mikveh.
chunks.st: but for eating sacrificial food one must immerse one’s hands in purification waters, such as those of a ritual bath.

chunks.en: And for the parah adumah water, if his hands became tamei,
chunks.st: And with regard to one who wishes to touch the purification waters of the red heifer used for sprinkling, concerning which the Sages ordained further measures of sanctity, if one’s hands were rendered impure
chunks.stMore: even by rabbinical ritual impurity, which usually only renders the hands impure,

words.note: The special water made with the ashes of the parah adumah.

chunks.en: his whole body becomes tamei.
chunks.st: his entire body is rendered impure, and he must immerse himself in a ritual bath.

summary: When a person goes to the mikveh, he becomes tahor only for the level of holy food he had in mind. If he had in mind a holier level, he may also eat the less holy foods.
stIntro: The mishna continues to list additional differences between various levels of ritual purity:

chunks.en: Someone who toveled for regular food and is counted tahor for regular food
chunks.st: If one immersed for the purpose of eating non-sacred food, he assumes a presumptive status of ritual purity for non-sacred food,

words.note: Dips in a mikveh to become tahor.

chunks.en: may not eat maaser.
chunks.st: and it is prohibited for him to eat tithes,
chunks.stMore: as he did not purify himself with the intention of eating tithes.

chunks.en: If he toveled for maaser and is counted tahor for maaser,
chunks.st: If one immersed to eat tithes, he assumes a presumptive status for tithes,

chunks.en: he may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: but he is prohibited from eating teruma.

chunks.en: If he toveled for terumah
chunks.st: If one immersed for teruma,

chunks.en: and is counted tahor for terumah,
chunks.st: he assumes a presumptive status for teruma,

chunks.en: he may not eat korbanos.
chunks.st: but he is prohibited from eating sacrificial food.

chunks.en: If he toveled for korbanos and is counted tahor for korbanos,
chunks.st: If he immersed for sacrificial food, he assumes a presumptive status for sacrificial food,

chunks.en: he may not touch the parah adumah water.
chunks.st: but he is prohibited from coming in contact with the purification waters.

chunks.en: If he toveled for something stricter,
chunks.st: The principle is as follows: One who immersed to eat a food in a stringent category

chunks.en: he may have something less strict.
chunks.st: is permitted to eat a food in a lenient one.

chunks.en: If he toveled but did not have in mind to become tahor,
chunks.st: Another principle: One who immersed without the intention to assume a presumptive status of ritual purity, i.e., one who immersed but did not intend to purify himself,

chunks.en: it is as if he did not tovel.
chunks.st: it is as though he has not immersed at all.

summary: People who keep a higher level of tahara must be careful with the clothes of people who keep a lower level. Even the clothes of very careful tzaddikim were counted as tamei for holier things.

chunks.en: The clothes of an am ha'aretz are tamei with midras for perushim.
chunks.explain: Perushim are people very careful about tahara.
chunks.st: The garments of an am ha’aretz, one who is not careful with regard to the laws of ritual purity, are considered impure with the ritual impurity imparted by the treading of a zav. That is considered a primary level of impurity for individuals who are scrupulous with regard to impurity [perushin].

words.note: Am ha'aretz: a person who is not careful about tumah and tahara.
A strong kind of tumah, like a seat a zav sat on.

chunks.en: The clothes of perushim are tamei with midras for those who eat terumah.
chunks.st: The garments of perushin are considered impure by the treading of a zav for priests who eat teruma;

chunks.en: The clothes of those who eat terumah are tamei with midras for korbanos.
chunks.st: the garments of those who eat teruma are considered impure by the treading of a zav for those who eat sacrificial food;

chunks.en: The clothes of those who eat korbanos are tamei with midras for the parah adumah water.
chunks.st: and likewise the garments of those who eat sacrificial food are considered impure by the treading of a zav for those dealing with the preparation of the purification waters.

chunks.he: יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר הָיָה חָסִיד שֶׁבַּכְּהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: Yosef ben Yoezer was the most pious of the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The mishna relates: Yosef ben Yo’ezer was the most pious member of the priesthood
chunks.stMore: and was extremely careful to eat teruma in a state of ritual purity,

chunks.en: and still his cloth was tamei with midras for korbanos.
chunks.st: and yet his cloth was considered impure by the treading of a zav for those who ate sacrificial food.

chunks.en: Yochanan ben Gudgeda ate
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda would eat non-sacred food

chunks.en: his regular food as carefully as korbanos all his life,
chunks.st: while following the laws of ritual purity for sacrificial food all his days,

chunks.en: and still his cloth was tamei with midras for the parah adumah water.
chunks.st: and nevertheless his cloth was considered impure by the treading of a zav for those preparing the purification waters.
